# How Lead Lab access and approval work
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

Lead Lab separates registration from access. Registration creates a participant record. Administrator approval grants entry to the private learning portal.

This separation prevents a person from reaching sessions, materials, Q&A, or calendar content simply by creating an account. A pending account can sign in only to see its review status. A revoked account is signed out when it tries to use protected portal features.

Email verification is part of the target-state approval rule. Local development may temporarily bypass it, but that does not change the rule for staging or production.

Administrators are the access decision-makers in the application. When a participant registers, active administrators receive an email alert to review the request. Approval changes the participant to active access. Revocation disables access without deleting the record, so restoration remains possible.

This is why the portal uses both an access status and an active flag: access is checked on the server for every protected route, not only in the browser interface. For the exact states and transitions, see the [access state machine](../architecture/state-machine.md#access-status).
